set.body:
Raised for Epic 9, which will certify on the current state.

certification-report.md asserts a complete package check with no errors or warnings and a single administrative CRAN-incoming note, from the command recorded at line 169:

  R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual ../effectagram_0.0.0.9000.tar.gz

That claim is attached to HEAD, b5d9a33. Since then the package has changed substantially and the check has not been re-run:

  untracked R files    20   (10708 lines)
  modified tracked     40
  new man pages        43
  no .Rcheck directory anywhere, no source tarball

So the strongest external quality claim in the repository currently describes a package that no longer exists. Everything added since - support-index, metric, metric-learning, relation-fit, residual-statistics, crossnobis, geometry-plan, format-results - is outside its scope, along with 43 new Rd files that have never been through Rd validation, cross-reference checking, or usage-vs-argument agreement.

WHY THIS MATTERS SPECIFICALLY FOR EPIC 9

Epic 9 closes the statistical 0.1 gate. The test suite is green (1819 pass, 0 fail, 0 error, 0 warn as of this pass), but testthat does not check: Rd syntax and completeness, usage sections matching formals, undocumented arguments, S3 method registration consistency, NAMESPACE/collate coherence, non-ASCII, or the CRAN-incoming checks the existing claim rests on. The 26 new S3method entries and 43 new Rd files are exactly the surface R CMD check exists to police, and none of it has been checked.

There is also a specific risk worth naming: the certification report at line 210 records that a previous rerun exposed a real namespace note - five internal head() calls lacking an importFrom. That is precisely the class of defect a suite cannot see and a check can, and it recurred once already.

RECOMMENDATION

Re-run R CMD check --as-cran before Epic 9 records any certification, and have the report cite the check output and the commit it was run against rather than inheriting the previous claim. If the intent is to keep the existing wording, the report should say explicitly which commit it describes and that later work is uncertified.

I did not run the check myself: R CMD build writes a tarball into the working tree, and doing that uninvited while the session is active risks colliding with in-flight work.
set.title: R CMD check has not been run since the certification claim; ~10.7k new lines and 43 new man pages since
